findings.text: The guard the change adds is bypassable one stage later, on an input the node's own tests cannot construct, and the bypass reproduces the exact outcome the node was dispatched to prevent. VERDICT: MUST-FIX. The population gate sits at export.py:2792-2822, BEFORE the `if not skip_gate:` gate block at :2824. It judges `candidates` as returned by `_classify_export_population`, so it is blind to every candidate Gate C (`score_thresholds`) or RC-mode Gate B (`grammar_parse_failure`) removes afterwards. Gate C always reports `GateResult(gate=GATE_C, passed=True, ...)` (export.py:1253) no matter how many candidates it filters, so a population that is fully excluded AFTER the gate reaches the catalog write with nothing in it. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT, measured at the integrated head 5fbf21830: one candidate `low_score_name` with `reviewer_score_name=0.10`, otherwise a normal accepted/valid row carrying a producing-source flag, exported with `min_score=0.65, skip_gate=False, gate_scope='domain', domain='general'`. Result: `all_gates_passed: True`, `exported_count: 0`, gates `[('catalog_status', True), ('export_population', True), ('graph_tests', True), ('score_thresholds', True), ('cross_field_consistency', True), ('divergence_detection', True), ('identity_token_collision', True), ('exclusion_accounting', True)]`, and `catalog.yml written: True`. The published catalog reads `candidate_count: 1, published_count: 0, domains_included: []`. That is byte-for-byte the shape the node's own base quote calls the defect - `all_gates_passed True, exported_count 0 and catalog_written True` - and because every gate passes, `_run_export_cli` (cli/sn.py:4458-4463 `if not report.all_gates_passed: ... raise SystemExit(1)`) exits 0 and a release script proceeds on an empty catalog. WOULD THE NODE'S OWN TESTS CATCH IT: no, structurally. Both new run_export tests go through `_run_fixture_export`, which passes `skip_gate=True` (tests/standard_names/test_export_exclusion_ledger.py:106-110), so Gate C never runs in the harness and the post-gate population is never non-trivially different from the pre-gate one. My probe had to bypass that harness to reach the input. REPAIR: re-evaluate the same emptiness predicate after the gate block (immediately before the `# 5.`/manifest write), or move the refusal to a check on `exported_count == 0` against a non-empty `total_candidates`, so the property the commit subject claims - refuse an export with nothing to publish - holds at every stage that can empty the population, not only the first. Log: /home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/runs/r-20260921T085222284241-review-of-an-unjudgeable-candidate-is-refused-not-published/probe_postgate_empty.log

The early return misreports the manifest cohort: a report written on the refusal path asserts `manifest_size: 0` for a caller that handed in N sources. VERDICT: not MUST-FIX (the export is blocked, so nothing is published), but it is a real misreport and the fence asks specifically whether the early return skips report content a caller needs. The answer is yes, for exactly one caller shape. `manifest_sources` reconciliation runs at export.py:3232-3295, roughly four hundred lines AFTER the new `return report` at :2822. The serialised report derives its manifest size from the records that reconciliation would have produced - `"manifest_size": len(self.source_disposition_records)` (export.py:445) - so the persisted `.export_report.json` positively states `{"manifest_size": 0, "accounted": 0, "rows": []}` when the caller supplied a non-empty manifest, and the `manifest_source_accounting` gate that would have refused the mismatch (`"type": "manifest_source_accounting_mismatch"`, export.py:3282-3288) never appears in `gates` at all. A reader of that report cannot distinguish `no manifest was supplied` from `a manifest of N was supplied and every row went unreconciled`. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT: `run_export(staging, review_batch=['a','b'], manifest_sources=[{...a...},{...b...}])` where both batch members carry `validation_status != 'valid'` (or are retired). `total_candidates` is 2, `candidates` is empty, `fully_excluded_population` fires, and the written report claims manifest_size 0 against a handed-in manifest of 2. MITIGATING: this is an inherited shape rather than an invention - the pre-existing null-catalog-status early return at export.py:2735-2746 has the identical defect - but this change extends it from a data-corruption input (null status) to a routine one (a scoped cut whose members are all excluded), which is how often it will now be seen. REPAIR: either reconcile `manifest_sources` before the population gate, or have the population-gate issue carry `manifest_size: len(manifest_sources or [])` so the report never states an unmeasured zero as a measurement.

`sn preview` now serves a STALE catalog while reporting a fresh export of zero names. VERDICT: not MUST-FIX; low severity, off the release path, and partly inherited. cli/sn.py:4535 calls `run_export(staging_dir=staging_path, force=True)` and then reads only `report.exported_count`; it never inspects `all_gates_passed`. The new gate returns before any write and is correctly insensitive to `force` (it sits above every force/skip_gate branch, which is the right call - I checked that neither flag bypasses it). CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT: a staging directory holding a `catalog.yml` from an earlier successful export, plus a graph state in which every identity is excluded. `imas-codex sn preview` prints `Exported 0 names`, the `if not catalog.is_file()` guard at :4543 passes because the OLD file is still there, and MkDocs serves the previous cut as if it were the one just exported. Before this change the same run overwrote the file with an empty catalog, which was worse in a different way (it published nothing but at least did not present old content as new). The same reasoning applies to the pre-existing null-status return, so this is a widening rather than a new hole. REPAIR: have the preview path check `report.all_gates_passed` and refuse, rather than falling through to a file-existence test that an old artifact satisfies.

The two new run_export tests index the persisted gate list positionally, so they will start asserting against the wrong gate the moment another gate is inserted ahead of them. VERDICT: not MUST-FIX; a test-durability note. `assert persisted["gates"][1]["issues"] == population_gate.issues` (tests/standard_names/test_export_exclusion_ledger.py, both new run_export tests) depends on `export_population` being the second gate appended, which holds only because `catalog_status` happens to be appended first at export.py:2734. CONCRETE TRIGGERING INPUT: add any gate between the status gate and the population gate - for instance the manifest reconciliation this review recommends moving earlier - and `gates[1]` becomes that gate; the comparison then fails for a reason unrelated to the property under test, or, if the new gate happens to carry the same issues list, passes vacuously. The tests already select the in-memory gate correctly by name (`next(gate for gate in report.gate_results if gate.gate == "export_population")`); the persisted assertion should use the same selection rather than an index.

justifications.durability: Split. The name_stage invariant is durable: one construction site, one caller, no fallback or except path that builds a candidate map, and a `not in` key test rather than a `.get()` whose default would re-open the hole - the same shape the adjacent `_validation_observed_at is None` and `_has_docs_review is False` branches already use, so it reads as native. On the fence's wave question - does the new invariant hold at EVERY construction site - the answer for the eligibility invariant is yes. For the population invariant it is no, and that is finding 1: the invariant has exactly one placement and the property it names can be violated at two later stages with no equivalent check. The guard is at least not bypassable by flag - I checked `force` and `skip_gate` both, and the gate sits above every branch either one controls, so neither lets a caller through; that is the right placement decision and consistent with the null-status gate above it. Against that, `report.gate_failures = 1` is an assignment rather than an increment, which is harmless here only because no gate has run yet - it is a latent misreport if the gate is ever moved down, which finding 1's repair may do. The new tests' positional `persisted["gates"][1]` (finding 4) is the other durability cost. Nothing else asserts the aperture of the new guard, so the third wave question - does any existing test assert the behaviour the change replaced - answers no for both halves: I found no test asserting a name_stage-less candidate is eligible and none asserting an empty or fully-excluded export writes a catalog.
justifications.evidence: Strong, and honest in the way that is hardest to fake. Both negative-control logs name their mutation on line 1 verbatim - `NEGATIVE CONTROL MUTATION: admit a candidate when the name_stage key is absent.` and `NEGATIVE CONTROL MUTATION: do not stop export when the export population gate fails.` - and each produces exactly the red it should: 1 failed for the first, 2 failed for the second, naming the three new tests. So the answer to `can the change be inverted with the suite still green` is no, demonstrated rather than asserted. I verified the suite delta independently rather than reading it from the manifest: the base and after logs' own totals lines read `21 failed, 7515 passed, 8 skipped, 326 deselected, 3 errors` and `21 failed, 7518 passed, 8 skipped, 326 deselected, 3 errors`, and diffing the sorted FAILED/ERROR node-id sets returns no difference (the one diff line my first grep produced was a captured `ERROR imas_codex...` log line, not a node id). Zero added failures, three added passes. The tests also assert the right thing: `assert not (tmp_path / "catalog.yml").exists()` pins the artifact rather than only the flag, which is what makes the inversion detectable. Deduction, small: no test drives a name_stage-less candidate through `run_export`; the guard is exercised only at the classifier. Given the production trigger is the batch branch, a run_export-level test over a batch member lacking the property would have been the one that could have failed.
justifications.fit: The change is written in the file's own idiom and inherits that idiom's one weakness. The population gate is a near-exact copy of the null-catalog-status gate twenty lines above it - same `GateResult` construction, same `all_gates_passed = False; gate_failures = 1`, same `staging_path.mkdir(...); _write_export_report(...); return report` tail - so a reader who knows one knows the other, and the new `GATE_EXPORT_POPULATION` constant is declared beside its siblings. `ExclusionRecord(stage="eligibility", reason=..., detail=...)` matches every other row the classifier emits, and the reason string is free-form here (there is no enumerated vocabulary for export exclusion reasons; `EXCLUSION_REASONS` in core/exclusions.py governs an unrelated mappings surface), so nothing downstream needed updating. The inherited weakness is that the early-return template skips the manifest reconciliation and therefore writes an unmeasured zero as if it were a measurement (finding 2), and a caller that reads only `exported_count` - `sn preview` - falls through to a stale artifact (finding 3). Both are the template's, not the author's invention, but this change makes them reachable on a far more ordinary input than the template's original one.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Half the stated goal holds without reservation and half does not. The missing-name_stage half is exactly right: export.py:828-836 replaces the fail-open `eligible.append(candidate); continue` with a named `eligibility_input_incomplete` exclusion, and the removed comment's premise does not survive inspection - `_classify_export_population` has exactly ONE non-test caller in the package, `run_export` at export.py:2747, whose input comes only from `_fetch_export_population`. So the fence's first specific question - is there a production caller that legitimately passes a pre-filtered projection without name_stage and is now refused - answers NONE EXISTS. The refusal is nevertheless reachable in production rather than fixture-only: the batch branch of the population query is `(sn.name_stage = 'approved' OR sn.id IN $batch)` (export.py:629), so a batch member with no `name_stage` property at all satisfies the predicate through the id clause, and the `sn {.*, ...}` map projection (export.py:699) omits a property the node does not carry. That identity was previously emitted into the catalog unjudged and is now a named ledger row. The population half does not hold as stated. `blocks an export whose population is empty or fully excluded` is true only for the pre-gate population; the same publish-nothing outcome survives Gate C and, in RC mode, Gate B, and I measured it writing catalog.yml with all gates passing (finding 1). On the fence's second question - does the fully-excluded refusal block a scoped or dry-run export whose report was itself the intended deliverable - the report IS still written (`_write_export_report` precedes the return at :2821, and both new tests read the persisted `.export_report.json`), so the deliverable is not lost; but a `--gate-only` or `--domain` dry run over an empty scope now returns a report carrying only two gates and a failing verdict where it previously carried the full gate chain, and the CLI turns that into SystemExit(1). I judge that acceptable rather than a defect - a gate result over zero candidates is vacuous - but it is a behaviour change a release script may notice.
justifications.scope_discipline: Clean. Both commits touch only the four declared write paths: 12f028f2b is `imas_codex/standard_names/export.py` plus `tests/standard_names/test_export_exclusion_ledger.py`, and 4b8778a8b is `docs/evidence/archive/unbound-source-backlog-landed.html` plus `docs/plans/unbound-source-backlog.html`. No stray edit, no generated file staged, no adjacent repair folded in. The 24 pre-existing reds in `tests/standard_names` - which include the very fixture harness this file uses, `test_export_ledger_closes_over_fixture_population` - were left alone and reported rather than triaged, which is correct for a fenced node and is also why my own first probe attempt was mis-shaped: the shared `_candidate` fixture predates the producer-evidence projection keys, so a naive candidate is excluded as `no_producing_source` before it ever reaches a gate. The worker did not paper over that. Commits carry a conventional subject and a body, no plan labels, no attribution.
